description:
Problem: .github/workflows/oracle-review.yml is a no-op notification. Its permission-less review-event job runs on pull_request_review submitted, edited and dismissed (oracle-review.yml:5-7; the run name carries the action, :3), and the oracle-gate workflow_run bridge (oracle-gate.yml:22-24 subscribes to oracle-verdict and oracle-review; the bridge job is :147-177) turns each completion into a gate dispatch. It was kept because oracle-verdict runs started by a comment, dispatch or schedule carry develop's tip SHA, so their completion cannot be mapped to a PR. Since #3436, oracle-verdict's post job dispatches oracle-gate for the PR and head right after posting its review (oracle-verdict.yml:996-1000 posts the review, :1002-1011 dispatches the gate). That post job is the only place oracle reviews are posted. The gate reads the pull request, changed files, the policy, oracle reviews including each review's current body, oracle threads, the base-change date and stand-in comments (oracle_gate.py:128-143; oracle_review_check.py:122-180); it does not read human reviews. The notification's only unique inputs are therefore an edit or a dismissal of an oracle review by someone other than the oracle. It costs a workflow run plus a bridge run per review (62 oracle-review runs in the 2.6 hours after #3429 merged), and a pull request already controls it: GitHub runs the copy in the PR's test merge, so a PR can delete or alter it.

Outcome: oracle-review.yml deleted; the gate bridge subscribes to oracle-verdict only; tests and docs describe the verdict's dispatch as the review-event path and the sweep as the refresh for review edits and dismissals.

Decision gates (queries are in context):
1. Evidence window (enforced by not_before). For every oracle-verdict run since 2026-10-25T05:38Z whose post job's 'Post the findings review' step concluded success: the 'Dispatch the gate for the reviewed head' step concluded success, and an oracle-gate workflow_dispatch run for that PR started after it and posted a status on that head. Record counts and run IDs. A missed or failed dispatch stops this item: file a defect for the dispatch path and make this item need it.
2. Load-bearing check. For each oracle-gate bridge run started by an oracle-review completion in the window, find a dispatch-started gate run for the same PR and head at or before it. If any bridge-started gate run had no such match and changed the posted oracle-gate state, stop and record which one.
3. Same-head flip. Record at least one same-head success-to-non-success oracle review followed, through the dispatch path, by an oracle-gate failure newer than the review. If none happens naturally, record 'not observed'; never manufacture verdicts or reviews to produce one.
4. Review edits and dismissals by others. Re-verify at implementation time that the gate counts only oracle reviews (oracle_review_check.py decide and _is_oracle) and that no repository code edits or dismisses reviews (no PUT, PATCH or dismissals call on pulls/*/reviews under .github and _project/scripts). List every oracle-review run in the window titled 'oracle-review (edited)' or 'oracle-review (dismissed)' with its triggering actor and PR. If any run's actor is the oracle App, or is not the author of a human review on that PR, an oracle review may have been edited or dismissed: stop and record it. Otherwise proceed only with the owner's recorded acceptance that an edit or dismissal of an oracle review by another account refreshes oracle-gate at the next sweep, within the bound measured by the sweep-cadence change.
5. Keep the bridge's oracle-verdict entry. Removing it is out of scope.

Scope:
- Delete .github/workflows/oracle-review.yml and tests/unit/workflows/test_oracle_review_workflow.py; remove that test's line from tests/unit/ledger_cutover_files.txt.
- .github/workflows/oracle-gate.yml: workflows: [oracle-verdict]; remove any bridge logic specific to oracle-review completions.
- Tests that load the file: test_oracle_gate_workflow.py:116-120 (assert the bridge subscribes to oracle-verdict only), test_oracle_verdict_workflow.py:17 and the test at :62-67 (keep the :349 assertion), test_release_pr_check_scope.py:28-30 (delete that test).
- Keep the .github/workflows/oracle-review.yml entries in .github/soundness-paths.txt:89 and .github/oracle-reviewers.yml:96 so a re-created file is still soundness-reviewed; test_soundness_paths.py:67 is a predicate case and stays.
- _project/scripts/oracle_review_check.py: remove the standalone checker command (_parse_args, main and the __main__ block) after LSP references show only tests call them; update tests/unit/scripts/test_oracle_review_check.py and the dev-loop-property-ledger rows that describe them.
- Docs: docs/internal/oracle-review-v2.md :617-641, :715-717 and :768-771; docs/internal/repo-admin-settings.md:70-71; docs/internal/soundness-drain.md:38-42; docs/internal/dev-loop-property-ledger.md:84 and :120; supersede the 'keeps its path and name' clause in _project/decisions/oracle-review-check-retired-2026-10-24.md:52-54.
- Leave unchanged: tests that use 'oracle-review' only as a sample check name (test_check_suites.py, test_pr_rerun.py, test_pr_landing.py, test_remote_closeout.py, test_pr_arm.py, the ruleset tests); comment-policy tests that reject oracle-review as evidence, including the fixture at test_comment_policy.py:2542; soundness_merge_digest.py's 'oracle-review' signal and its ORACLE_PATH test fixture; the 'oracle-review:' prefix of the gate's status messages.

Item guardrails: do not change oracle-verdict's posting or dispatch steps, the oracle_gate.py decision, the sweep or stand-in handling. Do not ask the owner to disable the workflow in repository settings. Land after the sweep-cadence change, which edits the same file and the same documentation paragraphs.

Common guardrails: work only in a linked worktree created by make worktree-create, after make agent-write-preflight; the primary clone is read-only. No SKIP or --no-verify, no stand-in approvals, no ruleset edits or bypasses, no raw gh pr merge. Do not change oracle-gate's App binding (integration 5201041), the oracle decision rule, or the native review-thread-resolution requirement. Do not close and reopen, mass-rerun or rebase other pull requests. No explanatory comments or docstrings in code; commits, PR bodies and docs carry no tracker item IDs or session labels.
